quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: Which clothing item will NOT reduce injuries in a crash?

options.text: Heavy shoes
Full-length pants
Shorts
Full-fingered gloves

questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: To reduce injury risk, wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Use durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket or pants, what should you look for?

options.text: Items made of leather
Items made of polyester
Items made of light materials
Items that are dark-colored

questions.correctAnswerText: Items made of leather
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to cover your arms and legs while riding. Leather provides the highest level of protection.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright
Slow down and lean the motorcycle
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and cross it as slowly as possible.

questions.question: Which surface provides GOOD traction?

options.text: Wet pavement
Dry pavement
Lane markings
Snow

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all provide poor traction. Dry pavement is safer for motorcycles.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good clothing choice for riding?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles
Leather gloves
A baseball cap to cover your hair

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair
questions.explanation: For protection, wear a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, ankle-covering boots or shoes, and durable gloves. Do not rely on a baseball cap alone.

questions.question: What is true about a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: It restricts side vision
It can greatly reduce head injury severity
It is usually uncomfortable
It makes motorcycle control more difficult

questions.correctAnswerText: It can greatly reduce head injury severity
questions.explanation: A helmet greatly improves your chances of avoiding serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet does not restrict your side vision.

questions.question: What is true about a leather jacket?

options.text: It can make a rider look cool
It is usually too warm to wear while riding
It provides protection in a crash
It should not be worn while riding

questions.correctAnswerText: It provides protection in a crash
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved leather jacket for protection. In warm weather, leather can help prevent dehydration. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool in hot weather.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is true about clothing when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: It should be loose enough to flap in the wind
It should not completely cover your arms or legs
You should not wear a jacket in warm weather
It can provide protection in a crash

questions.correctAnswerText: It can provide protection in a crash
questions.explanation: Good clothing can protect you in a crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Clothing should fit snugly without flapping but allow free movement.

questions.question: What is the best source of information for your motorcycle?

options.text: The owner's manual
A general book about motorcycles
Someone who has a different type of motorcycle
A television show about motorcycle riding

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual
questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?

options.text: With the right hand
With the left hand
With the right foot
With the left foot

questions.correctAnswerText: With the right hand
questions.explanation: On a motorcycle, the accelerator is at the right handgrip. You control it with your right hand.

questions.question: What should an approved helmet do?

options.text: Allow you to see far to the sides for safe riding
Look good
Not have a chin strap
Protect your hearing

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow you to see far to the sides for safe riding
questions.explanation: Many people think helmets limit your vision, but this is not true. Any U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet lets you see as far as you need to ride safely.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Helps other drivers see you
Is not allowed
Should only be used at night
Does not help you be seen

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps other drivers see you
questions.explanation: Reflective material on your vest or helmet makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it day and night.

questions.question: When riding past parked cars, what should you watch out for?

options.text: Drivers looking for a parking spot
Cars pulling out of parking spaces
Oncoming traffic
Noise

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling out of parking spaces
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked cars. A car may suddenly pull out from the curb or parking space into your path.

questions.question: What is Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) designed to do?

options.text: Stop the wheels from skidding and locking up
Stop brakes from working if the road is dry
Apply brakes by itself
Tell you when brake pads need replacing

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the wheels from skidding and locking up
questions.explanation: ABS stops the wheels from skidding and locking when you brake hard in a straight line. When electronic sensors detect wheel lock, the system releases brake pressure and then reapplies it to keep maximum stopping power.

questions.question: How does riding with a passenger affect your motorcycle?

options.text: It usually makes no difference
It is usually safe for new riders
It can change how the motorcycle handles
It helps riders practice different situations

questions.correctAnswerText: It can change how the motorcycle handles
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight, which changes how your motorcycle handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: If you drink one alcoholic drink and wait one hour before riding, what happens?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding
Your riding skills will not be affected
It is safe as long as you ride slowly
The alcohol may still affect your body

questions.correctAnswerText: The alcohol may still affect your body
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour, but this varies by person. It is safest to not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: How can you lower your crash risk?

options.text: Let other drivers know your plans with signals
Do not look ahead while riding
Wear dark clothes
Ride in parts of the lane where you are hard to see

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other drivers know your plans with signals
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to other drivers. Use signals, brake lights, and correct lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: At night
During the day
At dusk
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Always wear reflective and bright clothing when riding. Crashes happen day and night, so wear highly visible clothing at any time.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head to check your blind spot
Only use your mirrors
Point in the direction you are turning
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your risk of a crash?

options.text: Be visible to other drivers.
Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Always stay within one foot of another vehicle.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake lights, and lane position to show what you are doing. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: What should you do when riding an unfamiliar motorcycle?

options.text: Test the seat to make sure it is comfortable.
Assume the motorcycle is in good condition.
Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
Ride normally since most bikes are the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before you ride, get familiar with the bike. Practice the gear pattern and test the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Other drivers may go slowly while looking for a parking spot.
The road may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: Parked cars create hazards. A driver may pull out without looking and hit you. Car doors may open into your lane. Pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol and drugs are used together?

options.text: The effects are stronger than using either one alone.
The effects are less dangerous than using either one alone.
The effects are usually small.
The effects usually cancel each other out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects are stronger than using either one alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, make riding unsafe. Mixing medications with alcohol can be very dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do when riding with a passenger?

options.text: Assume they have ridden on a motorcycle before.
Do not assume they have experience and explain what they need to do.
Do not let them ask questions.
Do not explain anything since they are just a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not assume they have experience and explain what they need to do.
questions.explanation: Your passenger needs to know how to ride safely with you. Never assume they know what to do. Give your passenger clear instructions before every ride.
